deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematics. It is an archival note, not by Gauss. It is written in German by Ludwig Schlesinger and signed and dated 'Giessen 21. 5. 15', i.e. 21 May 1915, when he was editing Gauss's Nachlass for the Werke. A later pencil addition is signed by the Gauss archivist Theo Gerardy and dated 17/3 1954.

Content of the note, in translation:
- On the slip 'Zur Theorie des biquadr. Restes' 14 i, at the bottom of p. 4, there is a passage in Gauss's secret script. This is the cipher/tally symbols at the foot of the preceding folio 13, which the machine transcription marked as illegible.
- Gauss also used this script on a letter from Jacobi.
- See Borchardt's letter in Kapsel 118, kept with Gauss's letters to Alexander von Humboldt. Borchardt had found the key to the cipher.
- The deciphered text reads: 'Sagts dem armen alten Manne / morgen ist er jung und reich / auf dem Berge fällt die Tanne / sieben Fuss und eine Spanne / machen ihn dem Fürsten gleich'.
- The verse is attributed to Schmidt von Lübeck, i.e. the poet Georg Philipp Schmidt (1766-1849).
- Gerardy's addition cross-references Cod. Ms. Gauss Nr. 33a, S. 2.

Meaning of the verse: it is a riddle-poem whose answer is the coffin or grave. The fir felled on the mountain gives the coffin's wood. 'Seven feet and a span', the length of a coffin, make the poor old man equal to the prince: death equalises everyone.

Mathematical context (from the previous page, not this one): the ciphered line sits under Gauss's computation of a quantity M for the theory of biquadratic residues. That computation uses Eisenstein/Gauss-lemma-type sums of floor functions [kb/a] and congruences mod 16 and 32 in a, b with D = a^2 + b^2. The cipher itself is literary, not mathematical.

results.what: Archival note identifying and deciphering a line of Gauss's private cipher as a poem by Schmidt von Lübeck
results.usually_credited_to: Decipherment credited to C. W. Borchardt; note by L. Schlesinger (1915), addendum by T. Gerardy (1954)

deep.surprise_reason: The page holds no mathematics. It is an editor's note. Gauss's use of a private cipher and Borchardt's decipherment are known in the Gauss-Nachlass literature, so the page is of biographical and archival interest only.
transcription_corrections: 'bei den Briefe[?] von Gauss' should read 'bei den Briefen von Gauss'.
The poem's nouns are capitalised in the hand in places: 'Manne', 'Tanne', 'Spanne', 'Fürsten'. Lowercase in the transcription is acceptable as a reading of Schlesinger's hand.
The lines 'Vgl. auch Cod Ms Gauss Nr. 33 a S. 2' and 'Gerardy 17/3 1954' are a later pencil addition by Gerardy and are distinct from Schlesinger's ink note dated 'Giessen 21. 5. 15'.
